summary: The lecture details the Dutch East India Company's (VOC) formation in 1602 through amalgamation of six Dutch companies, its early exploration aided by stolen Portuguese maps, and establishment of trade posts in Southeast Asia (Amboina, Batavia) and India (Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Surat). It explains VOC's governance by 17 directors, world's first IPO via Article 10, expansionist policies under Jan Pieterszoon Coen, conflicts with Portuguese and English (Amboyna massacre, 1661 Bombay dowry, 1667 treaty), and final defeat by Travancore at the 1741 Battle of Colachel leading to Dutch exit from India.
points: Portuguese first Europeans in India; followed by Dutch, English, French East India Companies.
VOC formed 1602 by merging six Dutch companies on Johan van Oldenbarnevelt's advice.
Huyghen van Linschoten stole Portuguese nautical maps from Goa, enabling Dutch exploration.
Cornelis de Houtman's 1596-97 expedition reached East Indies; only 87 of 283 survived.
VOC charter 1602: Article 10 introduced world's first IPO, making it first multinational joint-stock company.
VOC governance: 17 directors (Heeren XVII) – 8 Amsterdam, 4 Middelburg, 1 each from Rotterdam, Delft, Hoorn, Enkhuizen, one rotating.
First Dutch factory in India at Masulipatnam (1605); Fort Geldria at Pulicat; later Surat, Chinsurah, Cochin.
1623 Amboyna massacre: Dutch executed 10 Englishmen, escalating Anglo-Dutch rivalry.
1661: Catherine of Braganza's dowry gave Bombay to English for £1, marginalizing Portuguese to Goa.
1741 Battle of Colachel: Travancore defeated Dutch; Treaty of Mavelikkara ended Dutch power in India.

check.q: When and how was the Dutch East India Company (VOC) formed?
opts: 1602 by royal decree of Dutch king
1602 by amalgamation of six companies on Johan van Oldenbarnevelt's suggestion
1605 by merger of Dutch and English companies

check.q: Which article of the VOC charter introduced the world's first initial public offering (IPO)?
What was the outcome of the 1741 Battle of Colachel for the Dutch East India Company?
opts: Dutch captured Travancore and expanded in India
Dutch signed Treaty of Mavelikkara, returned territories and were ousted from India
Dutch formed alliance with Travancore against English
Dutch retained control of Cochin and Malabar coast
